title: The perioperative care of patients with congenital heart defects undergoing non-cardiac surgery at a supraregional EMAH center - retrospective analysis
summary:
It is estimated that 300,000 patients in Germany have a congenital heart defect. Approximately 7-10/1,000 newborns are born with a heart defect. Of these, 90% now reach adulthood thanks to better diagnostics and the availability of surgical treatment, which is why there is an increase in anesthesiological care both outside of cardiac surgery and during childbirth. 
There is no valid guideline for the care of this particular patient group from an anesthesiology perspective. The European Society of Cardiology (ESC) recommends care in centers with special expertise.
We divide the group of patients with congenital heart defects to be examined into a) children with congenital heart defects undergoing non-cardiac surgery) adults with congenital heart defects (EMAH) undergoing non-cardiac surgery c) pregnant women from the EMAH group who underwent obstetric anesthesia. Our aim is to analyze the anesthesiological care of children and adults with congenital heart defects undergoing non-cardiac surgery and obstetric care, as there are currently no specific guideline recommendations.
In Germany, there is no anesthesiology registry data for this highly specialized patient group of congenital heart defects.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
People with congenital heart defects who can be divided into the following groups: a) children with congenital heart defects undergoing non-cardiac surgery, b) adults with congenital heart defects (EMAH) undergoing non-cardiac surgery and c) pregnant women from the EMAH group who received obstetric anesthesia care. The period should cover the years 2013-2023.
